title: What a real release looks like

scenes.headline: Real rescues leave a paper trail.
Named: Uporny, a 3-year-old Amur tiger
scenes.body: Caught after eating dogs near people in Khabarovsk province — a 'conflict tiger'.

scenes.headline: Checked before release
scenes.body: Health check, vaccinations and a hunting test at the Utyos Rehabilitation Center.

scenes.headline: Collared, then let go
scenes.body: Run by the regional forest department with WWF and the Amur Tiger Center.

scenes.headline: No paper trail? Don't share it.
scenes.body: Look for a named organisation, a place, a date and a follow-up.

caption:
This is what a verified animal release looks like.

Uporny ('stubborn' in Russian) was given a radio collar so his movements could be followed after release — the follow-up is part of the proof.

Source: WWF, 'Amur tiger released' (2015). Photos/video: Wikimedia Commons (credits on screen).
notes: AVOID format handled as the positive contrast: one verified release by named organisations (WWF's own CC footage), framed as a checklist for spotting fakes — not a rescue narrative of our own.
